title: IL SB2909: SCH CD-TEACHER EVALUATION-AI

obligations: Each school district shall establish a teacher evaluation plan ensuring each teacher in contractual continued service is evaluated at least once every 2 or 3 school years as provided (Sec. 24A-5).
Each school district shall establish a plan ensuring each teacher not in contractual continued service is evaluated at least once every school year (Sec. 24A-5, paragraph (1)).
Each teacher in contractual continued service rated 'needs improvement' or 'unsatisfactory' must be evaluated at least once in the following school year (Sec. 24A-5).

No later than September 1, 2022, each school district must establish a plan for teachers rated 'excellent' or 'proficient' to be evaluated at least once in 3 school years and implement an informal observation plan (Sec. 24A-5).

The evaluation plan must include components (a) through (o), including personal observation, consideration of attendance, planning, instructional methods, classroom management, and subject matter competency, rating, specification of strengths and weaknesses, copy in personnel file, professional development plan within 30 school days for 'needs improvement', remediation plan within 30 school days for 'unsatisfactory', consulting teacher participation, midpoint and final evaluations, reinstatement, and dismissal provisions (Sec. 24A-5).
If an evaluator uses an artificial intelligence tool, the name and specific purpose of the tool must be disclosed to the teacher being evaluated (Sec. 24A-5).
If a teacher uses an artificial intelligence tool, the name and specific purpose of the tool must be disclosed to the evaluator evaluating the teacher (Sec. 24A-5).
The joint committee under subsection (b-5) of Section 24A-4 shall determine how artificial intelligence tools may be used in accordance with paragraphs (a) through (o) (Sec. 24A-5).
prohibitions: An evaluator is prohibited from using an artificial intelligence tool to assign a numerical score or qualitative rating, such as 'excellent', 'proficient', 'need improvement', or 'unsatisfactory', for any component of a teacher's evaluation or any evaluation task that requires professional judgment (Sec. 24A-5).
A teacher is prohibited from using an artificial intelligence tool to generate evidence of professional practice that will be used by an evaluator to evaluate the teacher's performance (Sec. 24A-5).

What it does

Amends the Illinois School Code to regulate teacher evaluation plans, including prohibiting evaluators from using artificial intelligence tools to assign scores or ratings and prohibiting teachers from using AI tools to generate evidence of professional practice, while allowing AI for administrative tasks and requiring disclosure of AI tool use.

Who it applies to

  • School districts to which Article 24A of the School Code applies
  • Evaluators of teachers
  • Teachers
  • Joint committee under subsection (b-5) of Section 24A-4

Effective date

not stated in the text

Obligations

  • Each school district shall establish a teacher evaluation plan ensuring each teacher in contractual continued service is evaluated at least once every 2 or 3 school years as provided (Sec. 24A-5).
  • Each school district shall establish a plan ensuring each teacher not in contractual continued service is evaluated at least once every school year (Sec. 24A-5, paragraph (1)).
  • Each teacher in contractual continued service rated 'needs improvement' or 'unsatisfactory' must be evaluated at least once in the following school year (Sec. 24A-5).
  • No later than September 1, 2022, each school district must establish a plan for teachers rated 'excellent' or 'proficient' to be evaluated at least once in 3 school years and implement an informal observation plan (Sec. 24A-5).
  • The evaluation plan must include components (a) through (o), including personal observation, consideration of attendance, planning, instructional methods, classroom management, and subject matter competency, rating, specification of strengths and weaknesses, copy in personnel file, professional development plan within 30 school days for 'needs improvement', remediation plan within 30 school days for 'unsatisfactory', consulting teacher participation, midpoint and final evaluations, reinstatement, and dismissal provisions (Sec. 24A-5).
  • If an evaluator uses an artificial intelligence tool, the name and specific purpose of the tool must be disclosed to the teacher being evaluated (Sec. 24A-5).
  • If a teacher uses an artificial intelligence tool, the name and specific purpose of the tool must be disclosed to the evaluator evaluating the teacher (Sec. 24A-5).
  • The joint committee under subsection (b-5) of Section 24A-4 shall determine how artificial intelligence tools may be used in accordance with paragraphs (a) through (o) (Sec. 24A-5).

Prohibitions

  • An evaluator is prohibited from using an artificial intelligence tool to assign a numerical score or qualitative rating, such as 'excellent', 'proficient', 'need improvement', or 'unsatisfactory', for any component of a teacher's evaluation or any evaluation task that requires professional judgment (Sec. 24A-5).
  • A teacher is prohibited from using an artificial intelligence tool to generate evidence of professional practice that will be used by an evaluator to evaluate the teacher's performance (Sec. 24A-5).

Penalties and enforcement

The State Board of Education adopts rules for evaluation plans; the joint committee under subsection (b-5) of Section 24A-4 determines how artificial intelligence tools may be used. No specific penalties or private right of action for artificial intelligence misuse are stated in the text (Sec. 24A-5).

How it affects AI deployment

  • Evaluators cannot use AI tools to assign scores or ratings for evaluation components requiring professional judgment; AI may be used only for administrative tasks (Sec. 24A-5).
  • Teachers cannot use AI tools to generate evidence of professional practice; AI may be used only for administrative tasks (Sec. 24A-5).
  • Any AI tool used by an evaluator or teacher must have its name and specific purpose disclosed to the other party (Sec. 24A-5).
  • The joint committee determines permissible AI uses within the evaluation plan (Sec. 24A-5).

Notable exemptions

  • This Section does not apply to teachers assigned to schools identified in an agreement entered into between the board of a school district operating under Article 34 and the exclusive representative of the district's teachers in accordance with Section 34-85c (Sec. 24A-5).
  • Nothing in this Section or Section 24A-4 prevents immediate dismissal of a teacher for deficiencies deemed irremediable or for actions injurious to or endangering the health or person of students, or prevents dismissal or nonrenewal of teachers not in contractual continued service for any reason not prohibited by applicable employment, labor, and civil rights laws (Sec. 24A-5).

Compliance steps

  • Establish a teacher evaluation plan that complies with Section 24A-5 and any rules adopted by the State Board of Education (Sec. 24A-5).
  • Ensure evaluators do not use AI tools to assign numerical scores or qualitative ratings for evaluation components requiring professional judgment; allow AI only for administrative tasks (Sec. 24A-5).
  • Ensure teachers do not use AI tools to generate evidence of professional practice; allow AI only for administrative tasks (Sec. 24A-5).
  • Require disclosure of the name and specific purpose of any AI tool used by an evaluator or teacher (Sec. 24A-5).
  • Have the joint committee under subsection (b-5) of Section 24A-4 determine how AI tools may be used in accordance with paragraphs (a) through (o) (Sec. 24A-5).
  • Include all required evaluation plan components (a) through (o) (Sec. 24A-5).
